question: Show Lacrivia abandonment by territory over the last 13 weeks so district managers can plan rep coaching.
answer:
Over the last 13 weeks, 6.4% of Lacrivia claims were abandoned (334 of 5,201 claims), and the territories are fairly close together. Most territories fall between 5.5% and 8.2%. With only 8–28 abandoned claims per territory, most of these gaps are within normal random variation. Use this to decide where to take a closer look, not to rank reps.

**By district** (weeks ending 3 Jul – 25 Sep 2026)

| District | Claims | Abandoned | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-05 | 821 | 59 | **7.2%** |
| D-01 | 984 | 70 | **7.1%** |
| D-02 | 753 | 49 | 6.5% |
| D-03 | 1,123 | 70 | 6.2% |
| D-06 | 744 | 45 | 6.0% |
| D-04 | 776 | 41 | 5.3% |
| **National** | **5,201** | **334** | **6.4%** |

**By territory** (highest rate first)

| Territory | Claims | Abandoned | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-01 T2 (T012) | 255 | 21 | 8.2% |
| D-06 T4 (T064) | 113 | 9 | 8.0% |
| D-05 T2 (T052) | 361 | 28 | 7.8% |
| D-01 T3 (T013) | 232 | 17 | 7.3% |
| D-02 T1 (T021) | 193 | 14 | 7.3% |
| D-04 T4 (T044) | 196 | 14 | 7.1% |
| D-03 T4 (T034) | 188 | 13 | 6.9% |
| D-05 T1 (T051) | 145 | 10 | 6.9% |
| D-01 T4 (T014) | 146 | 10 | 6.8% |
| D-02 T2 (T022) | 133 | 9 | 6.8% |
| D-03 T1 (T031) | 325 | 22 | 6.8% |
| D-05 T4 (T054) | 147 | 10 | 6.8% |
| D-06 T3 (T063) | 180 | 12 | 6.7% |
| D-05 T3 (T053) | 168 | 11 | 6.5% |
| D-01 T1 (T011) | 351 | 22 | 6.3% |
| D-02 T4 (T024) | 130 | 8 | 6.2% |
| D-02 T3 (T023) | 297 | 18 | 6.1% |
| D-06 T1 (T061) | 235 | 14 | 6.0% |
| D-03 T2 (T032) | 174 | 10 | 5.7% |
| D-03 T3 (T033) | 436 | 25 | 5.7% |
| D-04 T3 (T043) | 293 | 16 | 5.5% |
| D-06 T2 (T062) | 216 | 10 | 4.6% |
| D-04 T1 (T041) | 272 | 11 | 4.0% |
| D-04 T2 (T042) | 15 | withheld | withheld |

**Coaching takeaways**
- **Worth a look:** T012 (8.2%) and T052 (7.8%) are the busiest territories with the highest rates. Even so, a single territory's rate can easily move ±3–4 points by chance. So talk with the rep about access and support first; don't treat the number as a performance finding.
- **Possible good practice to share:** T041 (4.0%) and T062 (4.6%) are the lowest. T041 is the only one that is close to being meaningfully below the national rate.
- **T014 and T064** have 7 or fewer prescribers each, so their rates are especially unstable.
- **T042 is withheld:** it has one prescriber and 15 claims, so any rate would effectively show that one prescriber's patients' behaviour.
- **Week to week**, the national rate moved between 3.6% and 9.3%, peaking in the week ending 18 Sep (40 of 430). No territory shows a sustained trend.

**Data-use note:** Because this is going to the field, I've shown territory and district totals only. It includes no patient-level or prescriber-level abandonment detail, and I suppressed the one territory where a figure would point to a single prescriber. The numbers shouldn't be used to set incentive pay, and reps shouldn't use them to follow up with specific patients, prescriptions or pharmacies.

**Sources and definitions**
- **Abandonment rate:** the share of Lacrivia claims flagged as abandoned. The source is the patient-level claims table `RAW_3P.PATHPT_LVL`, used here only in totals. Lacrivia means both of its package codes (NDCs 99101010105 and 99101010110), taken from `CORE.PRODUCT`.
- **Territory:** each claim is assigned to its prescriber's territory in `CORE.PRESCRIBER`, and districts come from `CORE.TERRITORY`. All 5,201 claims matched and there were no duplicate rows.
- **Last 13 weeks:** weeks run Saturday to Friday, matching the weekly prescription data. The latest full week ends 25 Sep 2026. Claims dated 26–30 Sep (an incomplete week) are left out.

**Assumptions**
- I used the current official territory alignment, not the draft alignment in the sandbox (`SANDBOX.TERR_ALIGN_Q2_DRAFT`).
- The claim-level adjudication table has its own abandonment flag, but it has no prescriber on it, so it can't be broken out by territory.
- The abandonment flag in the data ends on 25 Sep. Late updates to that flag could still move the last week or two slightly.

sql.sql: select table_schema, table_name, column_name, comment from PHARMA_DEMO.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS where comment is not null

select min(clm_dt), max(clm_dt), count(*), count(distinct pat_key), abndn_flg, count(distinct prscrbr_me) from PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.PATHPT_LVL where prod_ndc11 in ('99101010105','99101010110') group by abndn_flg
select max(wk_end_dt), dayname(max(wk_end_dt)), count(distinct wk_end_dt) from PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY

select date_trunc('week', clm_dt+2)-2+6 as wk_end, count(*) n, sum(iff(abndn_flg='Y',1,0)) ab, round(ab/n*100,2) pct
from PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.PATHPT_LVL where prod_ndc11 in ('99101010105','99101010110') and clm_dt>='2026-05-01' group by 1 order by 1
select count(*), count(distinct prscrbr_me), count(distinct npi), sum(iff(terr_id is null,1,0)), count(distinct terr_id) from PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER
select abndn_flg, adj_stat, count(*) from PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.CLMLNS_ADJ where prod_ndc11 in ('99101010105','99101010110') group by 1,2 order by 1,2

with c as (
 select p.*, pr.terr_id from PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.PATHPT_LVL p left join PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER pr on p.prscrbr_me=pr.prscrbr_me
 where p.prod_ndc11 in ('99101010105','99101010110') and p.clm_dt between '2026-06-27' and '2026-09-25')
select t.district_id, coalesce(c.terr_id,'UNMAPPED') terr, t.terr_nm, count(*) claims, sum(iff(abndn_flg='Y',1,0)) ab, round(ab/claims*100,1) pct, count(distinct prscrbr_me) hcps
from c left join PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.TERRITORY t on c.terr_id=t.terr_id group by 1,2,3 order by 1,2

with c as (
 select p.*, pr.terr_id, t.district_id from PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.PATHPT_LVL p join PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER pr on p.prscrbr_me=pr.prscrbr_me join PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.TERRITORY t on t.terr_id=pr.terr_id
 where p.prod_ndc11 in ('99101010105','99101010110') and p.clm_dt between '2026-06-27' and '2026-09-25')
select district_id, count(*) claims, sum(iff(abndn_flg='Y',1,0)) ab, round(ab/claims*100,1) pct,
 (select count(*) from (select pat_key,clm_dt,prod_ndc11,prscrbr_me,plan_id,abndn_flg, count(*) from c group by all having count(*)>1)) dup_groups
from c group by rollup(district_id) order by 1
